title: Sell Mineral Rights in Midland, TX
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Midland, TX
metaDescription: Midland mineral owner? We buy Spraberry and Wolfcamp interests directly, reading your division order and nearby permits before quoting a number, no listing needed.
heroLead: Midland is the town the basin is named after in everyone's mind, and owning minerals under or near it usually means sitting on some of the most-drilled acreage in the country.
intro: Most Midland mineral tracts we look at trace to the same Spraberry and Wolfcamp development that's made this county the operational center of the whole Permian. Some interests here have been producing since the original Spraberry discovery in 1949, since re-completed and re-drilled with horizontal wells over the last decade and a half.

sections.heading: City growth versus mineral ownership
paragraphs: Midland has expanded a lot over the years, and plenty of mineral tracts that were open ranchland when the reservation was written now sit under subdivisions, office parks, or the airport corridor. That doesn't change your ownership under Texas law, mineral and surface estates stay separate, though it can complicate future drilling access on some sections.

sections.heading: What we check before quoting
paragraphs: We pull your division order alongside the Railroad Commission history for every wellbore on your unit, since a lot of Midland tracts have several stacked Wolfcamp benches producing under one surface location. We also check for recent permits on offset sections, given how much active development still runs through this county.

sections.heading: Why buyer competition is stronger here
paragraphs: Because Midland is where so many operators and mineral buyers are based, owners here tend to get more unsolicited offer letters than owners in surrounding counties. That's actually useful for you, more competition among buyers generally means it's worth comparing offers rather than settling for the first number that arrives.

faqs.question: Does it matter that my minerals are under the city now instead of open land?
faqs.answer: Not for ownership. Texas law keeps mineral and surface estates separate regardless of surface development, though it can affect future drilling access on some built-up tracts.

faqs.question: How do you handle a tract with several wells on it?
faqs.answer: We pull production history for every wellbore tied to your unit, since Midland acreage commonly has multiple Wolfcamp benches and the Spraberry stacked together.

faqs.question: How fast can a Midland sale close?
faqs.answer: Typically two to four weeks with clean title and a current division order. Interests needing heirship or title work take longer, and we'll be upfront about that timeline.

faqs.question: Why do I get so many unsolicited offer letters for my Midland minerals?
faqs.answer: This county has more mineral buyers active than most surrounding counties, given how much operator activity and headquarters presence there is here. It's worth comparing multiple offers before deciding who to sell to.
